question: Why did the Eastern and Western churches separate?

answers.label: Over Rome's authority: primacy of rule or of honor
Over doctrine, above all the filioque

overview.text: There was no single break. Tensions over Rome's authority go back to the third century, and the East ranked sees by the imperial capital, "New Rome".

The open quarrels came over the filioque added to the Western creed (see question 16) and over papal claims: Photius in 867, the mutual excommunications of 1054, the sack of Constantinople in 1204. Florence (1439) tried to reunite them on Rome's terms and failed.
In 1965 Paul VI and Athenagoras I together lifted the anathemas of 1054 and committed them to oblivion, though the division itself remained.

quotes.author: Firmilian of Caesarea
quotes.english: I am rightly angry at this open and plain folly of Stephen: he who boasts so of the place of his episcopate and claims to hold the succession of Peter, on whom the foundations of the Church were laid, brings in many other rocks and sets up new buildings of many churches.
quotes.original: ego in hac parte iuste indignor ad hanc tam apertam et manifestam Stephani stultitiam, quod qui sic de episcopatus sui loco gloriatur et se successionem Petri tenere contendit, super quem fundamenta ecclesiae collocata sunt, multas alias petrae inducat et ecclesiarum multarum noua aedificia constituat
quotes.context: Already in 256 an Eastern bishop rejected Rome's claim to settle a dispute for all churches.

quotes.author: Council of Constantinople (as Socrates reports)
quotes.english: Then they also issued a decree that the bishop of Constantinople should have the privileges of honor after the bishop of Rome, because it is New Rome.
quotes.original: Τότε δὴ καὶ ὅρον ἐκφέρουσιν, ὥστε τὸν Κωνσταντινουπόλεως ἐπίσκοπον τὰ πρεσβεῖα ἔχειν τῆς τιμῆς μετὰ τὸν Ῥώμης ἐπίσκοπον, διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτὴν νέαν Ῥώμην.
quotes.context: Ranking sees by the imperial capital, rather than by apostolic founding, set East and West on different paths. Rome rejected the canon, and the later canon 28 of Chalcedon.

quotes.author: Photius of Constantinople
quotes.work: Encyclical Letter to the Eastern Patriarchs
quotes.english: They tried to falsify the holy Creed ... by coining the new teaching that the Holy Spirit proceeds not from the Father only, but also from the Son
quotes.original: κιβδηλεύειν ἐπεχείρησαν ... τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον οὐκ ἐκ τοῦ Πατρὸς μόνον, ἀλλά γε καὶ ἐκ τοῦ Υἱοῦ, ἐκπορεύεσθαι καινολογήσαντες
quotes.context: The first Eastern charge sheet against Rome, sent to the other patriarchs in 867. The filioque heads the list of Latin errors: Photius is charging the Frankish missionaries in Bulgaria with falsifying the Creed itself.

quotes.author: Humbert of Silva Candida
quotes.english: Michael, a usurping patriarch, a neophyte ... and all their followers in the errors and presumptions named above: let them be anathema Maranatha ... with the devil and his angels
quotes.original: Michaél abusivus patriarcha neophytus ... et omnes sequaces eorum in praefatis erroribus et praesumptionibus, sint anathema Maranatha ... cum diabolo et angelis ejus
quotes.context: Laid on the altar of Hagia Sophia on 16 July 1054. Cerularius and his synod answered with their own anathemas days later; the mutual sentences were lifted only in 1965.

quotes.author: Niketas Choniates
quotes.english: Mules and pack animals, laden, were led in as far as the sanctuary of the church ... a wretched little woman, heaped with sins ... let out a loose and broken song
quotes.original: ἡμίονοί τε καὶ ὑποζύγια σεσαγμένα μέχρι τῶν ἀδύτων εἰσήγοντο τοῦ νεὼ ... γυναικάριόν τι σεσωρευμένον ἁμαρτίαις ... κεχλασμένον ἀφῆκε μέλος
quotes.context: A Byzantine official who lived through the sack of April 1204; his account is a chief reason 1204, more than 1054, fixed the separation in Greek memory. In the full passage the woman is seated on the patriarchal throne in Hagia Sophia. The 1835 scan is rough and some words are hard to read in it; the words quoted follow the standard printed text.

quotes.author: Council of Florence
quotes.english: to him was committed in blessed Peter the full power of tending, ruling and governing the whole church
quotes.original: to him was committed in blessed Peter the full power of tending, ruling and governing the whole church
quotes.context: The reunion decree, signed by the Byzantine emperor and most Greek bishops, accepted the filioque and Roman primacy. It was rejected in Constantinople and never took hold.

quotes.author: Paul VI and Athenagoras I
quotes.english: They likewise regret and remove both from memory and from the midst of the Church the sentences of excommunication which followed these events ... and they commit these excommunications to oblivion.
quotes.original: They likewise regret and remove both from memory and from the midst of the Church the sentences of excommunication which followed these events ... and they commit these excommunications to oblivion.
quotes.context: Read simultaneously in Rome and Istanbul on 7 December 1965, at the close of the Second Vatican Council. It lifted the mutual sentences of 1054, but it did not restore communion: the declaration itself says this gesture was not sufficient to end the old and more recent differences between the two churches (para. 5). quotes.author: Russian Orthodox Church (Moscow Patriarchate)
quotes.work: Position on the problem of primacy in the Universal Church
quotes.english: They also believed that primacy in honour accorded to the bishops of Rome is instituted not by God but men.
quotes.original: They also believed that primacy in honour accorded to the bishops of Rome is instituted not by God but men.
quotes.context: The Orthodox position on the root of the split.

source.edition: Moscow Patriarchate, Position on the problem of primacy in the Universal Church (2013)
